label: bad
seen: No measurement of this game exists; none was taken. I saw no score, band or tier of it or of its parent while building and labelling it; the parent's published verdicts in labelled-set.md §9 I did not open in this task.
claim: White never loses: it has a recipe under which it never loses; the other side's result is not claimed.
change: one: White's f- and g-pawns are replaced by two shrines (a new piece that never moves and shields its side's king and shrines next to it).
aim: Nothing in ordinary play leads a king onto its keep and holds it there: players castle, walk the king when the board empties, and lose it in the open, so play should be the parent's, decisive from both seats and of ordinary length. The draw is there only for a side that knows to sit.

proof.text: Each shrine (type `T`, no moves) carries a line of sight with effect `shield`, `whose` own, `affects` the king and the shrine, range 1 in all eight directions, `through`: a shielded piece cannot be taken and a shielded king is never in check (`pieces[].sight`). The two shrines stand side by side and never move, so each shields the other for the whole game, and a king standing next to either is never in check. The recipe (White): play e2-e4 and then Qe1-e2; never castle; once the queen has left, never move any white piece but the king onto e1 or f1; move the king only between f1 and e1. Under it the king stands on f1 or e1, both next to a shrine, so it is never in check and never checkmated, and the parent has no other way for White to lose. It must move only when White has no other legal move; then the other square holds none of White's pieces (the recipe keeps them off it), and if an enemy piece stands there the king may take it, since a king next to its shrine is never in check after the move: so the step is always legal and White is never without a move. Until the queen has left e1 (White's second move, always legal since White's king is never in check) White has other legal moves, so the king never has to move. Black has no shrine. Wins are reachable: in each line of `checks` a king leaves its shrine and is mated.

review.notes: The shrines shield each other and both e1 and f1; the black king can never stand on the other square (it would be next to White's king) and any other black piece there can be taken. No failure in 6,487 recipe-following playouts with over a million forced king steps.
